penetration_assumption: Denominator first, because it is the number that kills the naive sizing. This is NOT a 4,700-person market. Most residents eat in the mess/langar; only staff families cook. VERIFIED proxies over the live 12m at the retail POS: 2,039 bills contained a core kitchen spice (turmeric/chilli/coriander/garam masala); 10,894 bills contained atta. At 6-8 spice purchases per cooking household per year that is ~255-340 households; the atta line at 24-36 buys/yr gives ~300-450. I use ~350 cooking households (ESTIMATED). Per line: (1) CUMIN/JEERA POWDER, 2 facings, Rs 11,000/yr — assumption: a new ground-spice facing performs like the observed coriander-powder facings (Catch Dhania Rs 4,424, MDH Dhania Rs 4,164) rather than turmeric (Rs 10,318-16,042), lifted slightly because adjacent whole-jeera already sells Rs 66,811/yr across 7 SKUs, so the demand is proven and only the grind is absent. (2) ACHAR/PICKLE MASALA, 1-2 facings, Rs 5,000/yr — assumption: of ~350 cooking households, 15% (about 53) make pickle at home and buy one Rs 60-70 pack inside the May-Jun window; deliberately conservative because the "pickle spike" evidence turned out to be a warehouse artefact (see probe_evidence). (3) SAFFRON, 1 locked facing, Rs 4,400/yr — assumption: 5% of 350 households buy one 1g box at Rs 250/yr; marginal and theft-prone. (4) CHAI/TEA MASALA, Rs 11,000/yr — NOT an add, a REORDER: assumption is a properly stocked facing does ~250 bills at ~Rs 45 on a cold hill campus that drinks tea all day. (5) BIRYANI/PULAO MASALA, Rs 4,000/yr — reorder, small base. Total Rs 35,400/yr revenue = 0.05% of a Rs 7.67 Cr business. Gross margin applied is the ledger-derived 18.0%, NOT the 25-40% the demand research assumed, giving Rs 6,372/yr. Every rupee figure here is ESTIMATED; the states (absent vs dormant vs covered) are VERIFIED.

EVERY OTHER MUST-HAVE IS PRESENT AND SELLING at retail (live 12m): black pepper 22 SKUs Rs 1,06,266; hing 18 SKUs Rs 65,083; kasuri methi 18 Rs 51,459; chaat masala 6 Rs 39,350; black salt 8 Rs 24,822; sendha/rock salt 8 Rs 22,175; amchur 7 Rs 16,628; sonth 2 Rs 4,037. Cumin powder is the ONLY genuinely absent must-have. THE DORMANT LINES ARE AVAILABILITY, NOT ASSORTMENT — purchase+stock history proves it: Keya Chai Masala 90g bought 6 units ONCE (Apr-2023), sold 6 of 6, stock 0, never reordered. MTR Veg Pulao bought 9 (Mar-2024), sold 9 of 9, never reordered. Daawat Biryani Kit bought 6, sold 5. MTR Peas Pulao, Trust Sugar Cubes, Trust Suger Pouch, Trust Classic Sugar: NEVER PURCHASED — phantom listings. 100% sell-through on every trial buy that was actually made.
kill_reason: Not a kill, but the assortment framing is the wrong lens and the rupee gap is ~0.05% of turnover. The proof, all VERIFIED on the live window 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31 (data now runs to 2026-08-30; the frozen 2026-08-21 corpus is superseded): the 518 active spice/salt-sugar SKUs split into 95 selling AND in stock (Rs 8.91 L) · 111 that SOLD in 12m but are at ZERO stock across every warehouse today (Rs 6.92 L of proven demand) · 18 dead stock · 292 with no stock and no sales, of which 151 were NEVER PURCHASED ONCE in the entire database history. So 29% of the "active" range is fiction that was never a physical product, and 44% of category revenue sits on SKUs currently unbuyable. Adding a 519th SKU to that catalogue is worse than useless. Sizing the real problem: 62 spice SKUs with at least 30 days of selling history are at zero stock, average 122 DAYS OUT. Revenue foregone Rs 43,429/yr (conservative: annualised over 365 days) to Rs 1,48,532/yr (run-rate: annualised over each SKU's actual selling span); central ~Rs 95,000. Even the conservative FLOOR exceeds the entire Rs 35,400 assortment gap, and the central estimate is ~2.7x it, with no new listings and no new capital. The out-of-stock list is the category's own must-haves: Mdh Dhania Powder 100g (Rs 4,164/yr, last sold 2026-04-20), Catch Jeera 200g (Rs 15,545, last 2026-06-03), Mdh Termaric Powder 100g (Rs 12,126), Ruchi Ajwain (Rs 8,385), Catch Elichi Rs10 (Rs 8,820), Jivo Black Pepper 100g (Rs 6,720 — the parent company's own label, out since 2026-06-15). The demand research asks for cumin powder while ARY cannot keep whole cumin on the shelf. TWO EVIDENCE ERRORS IN THE PRIOR PASS THAT I CORRECTED: (a) the diff's headline argument for pickle masala — "category sales spike to Rs 2.68 L (May-26) / Rs 2.20 L (Jun-26) from a Rs 90k-140k baseline, i.e. the pickle window is real and unserved" — is a warehouse-mixing artefact. Splitting by warehouse: May-26 = Rs 1,65,691 Basement + Rs 1,02,506 retail; Jun-26 = Rs 1,16,853 Basement + Rs 1,02,687 retail. Retail POS ran Rs 88,941 (Sep) to Rs 1,02,687 (Jun), about +12-15%, not a 2-3x spike. The "spike" is the langar buying rice/atta/sugar in bulk and has nothing to do with pickle season. The pickle-masala rationale is therefore unproven, which is why I sized it at Rs 5,000 and not more. (b) MARGIN: the demand research assumed 25-40%. Derived from the live purchase ledger (PurchaseDetail.PurchaseCost vs realised rate, net of the 5% GST that FinalSaleAmount includes — IncludeInRate=true confirmed on sample lines), 164 SKUs covering 97.8% of retail category sales: TRUE SPICES + SALT = 18.0% GM (149 SKUs, Rs 6.75 L net revenue, Rs 1.21 L gross profit). SUGAR/GUD = MINUS 18.8% (15 SKUs, Rs 3.31 L net revenue, Rs 3.93 L cost, losing Rs 62,133/yr) — Raja Sugar 1Kg sells Rs 50.3 against Rs 61.0 cost on Rs 1.85 L of volume. The single largest rupee item in this category is not a missing SKU, it is a subsidised staple bleeding Rs 62k/yr, which is a pricing decision for the Trust, not a buying one.
top_skus: REORDER (highest value, zero listing cost) — the 62 proven sellers at zero stock, worth Rs 43k-1.49 L/yr: Mdh Dhania Powder 100 Gm (out since 2026-04-20), Catch Jeera 200 Gm (out since 2026-06-03), Mdh Termaric Powder 100Gm, Ruchi Ajwain 100 Gm, Catch Elichi Rs 10/-, Jivo Black Pepper 100 Gm, Mdh Sabzi Masala 100G, Savour Green Cardamom 3 Gm
REORDER — Keya Chai Masala 90 Gm (ProductID 0CSS): bought 6 units once in Apr-2023, sold 6 of 6, never reordered. Cold hill campus, tea all day. Rs 11,000/yr, already listed
ADD — Catch Jeera/Cumin Powder 100 Gm: the only genuinely absent must-have; sits beside Rs 66,811/yr of proven whole-jeera demand
ADD — MDH Jeera Powder 100 Gm: second facing, matches the existing MDH/Catch duopoly pattern on every other powder

DELIST — 151 spice SKUs never purchased once in database history, incl. Trust Sugar Cubes 500 Gm, Trust Suger Pouch 1Kg, Trust Classic Sugar 150 Pcs, Mtr Peas Pulao 250 Gm. They inflate the range count and hide the real stockouts
DO NOT ADD — premium/organic turmeric, palm/date jaggery, instant dry yeast, saffron beyond one locked facing, and any non-veg/tandoori masala (vegetarian Trust campus)
blockers: REPLENISHMENT IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, NOT SHELF OR CAPITAL. 62 proven sellers average 122 days out of stock and 100% of trial buys on dormant SKUs sold through without a reorder. Until a reorder trigger exists, any SKU added here becomes phantom listing number 152. This is the whole finding.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH HP. The rack runs on MDH + Catch + Ruchi + Sunil + Shiv Pujari + unbranded local. Everest — India's largest spice brand — has 3 SKUs at ARY and all are dormant, which points to a distributor who does not service this hill route rather than a buying choice. New lines must come from the existing MDH/Catch vans or they will not arrive.
MARGIN IS 18.0%, NOT 25-40%. Ledger-derived. Any plan built on the demand research's margin band overstates profit by roughly half.

SUGAR/GUD SELLS 21% BELOW COST, losing Rs 62,133/yr on Rs 3.42 L of volume. That is a Trust pricing/subsidy decision and it dwarfs the assortment gap. Do not extend this line (palm/date jaggery) without resolving the pricing question first.

STRUCTURAL CEILING ON THE CATEGORY. Spices are 2.06% of ARY revenue vs 6-10% for a typical kirana, because campus spice throughput is consumed by the mess as BOM (group 190 Raw Material, 149 per-gram recipe SKUs, zero sales value) and bought bulk through the Basement desk (Rs 5.09 L, 12 bills/yr). Only ~350 households cook. There is no large hidden retail demand to unlock.

LOOSE BY-GRAM SPICE COUNTER IS NOT NEW REVENUE. The 15 weight-priced '_L' SKUs exist but sell ONLY through Basement, exactly 5 bills each, all bulk mess indents (VERIFIED). A retail counter would mostly CANNIBALISE packaged sales: at 20% of the Rs 7.07 L true-spice retail switching and a ~15pp margin uplift it is ~Rs 21,000/yr of gross profit, not revenue, and the low-unit-price need is already served by Rs 5-10 sachets (Maggi Masala Magic Rs 45,570 is the #1 SKU by frequency). It also needs FSSAI open-food handling, dispensers, a scale and staff time.
SAFFRON IS THEFT-PRONE and needs a locked facing; at Rs 4,400/yr it likely does not repay the handling.

MEASUREMENT LIMITS: 97% of bills book to one anonymous cash account, so household counts are proxies (bill-frequency based), not customer counts. Payment-mode VALUE columns are unusable. SaleHeader has no cancel flag, so gross sales overstate slightly by return value.
